content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a significant role in the metabolism of various drugs. Rabeprazole can increase the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Tecovirimat, a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19, can increase the levels or effects of rabeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. However, it can also decrease the levels or effects of rabeprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is also a weak inducer of CYP3A4, so monitoring the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended when co-administered. Rabeprazole can increase the toxicity of theophylline through mechanisms unrelated to CYP enzymes. Prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) like rabeprazole may lead to hypochlorhydria, which can alter gastrointestinal motility, increasing peristalsis in the small intestine and decreasing it in the proximal colon. Monitoring for toxicity is essential. Rabeprazole can increase the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, triclabendazole can increase the levels or effects of rabeprazole by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole use, rechecking these levels after discontinuation of triclabendazole is recommended. Rabeprazole can decrease the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility through increased gastric pH, which reduces its bioavailability. The impact on efficacy is unknown, so caution and monitoring are advised. Acetazolamide can increase the levels or effects of rabeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Conversely, amobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of rabeprazole by influencing both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is also unknown. Anastrozole can increase the levels or effects of rabeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance remains unclear. Atazanavir can similarly increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Blessed thistle may reduce the effects of rabeprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism, though this interaction is theoretical and of unclear significance. Bortezomib can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor or unknown clinical significance. Bosentan can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Butabarbital and butalbital can also decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Rabeprazole can decrease cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is of unclear clinical significance. Cyclophosphamide can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Danazol can similarly increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Darifenacin may reduce the effectiveness of rabeprazole through theoretical mechanisms involving other antisecretory agents. Darunavir can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Dasatinib can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Devil's claw may reduce rabeprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, though this interaction is theoretical and of unknown significance. Dexamethasone can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Herbal DHEA can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Dronedarone can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Drospirenone can similarly increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Efavirenz can both increase and decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. The clinical significance of these opposing effects is unclear. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF does not appear to have clinically significant interactions with rabeprazole based on drug interaction studies. Erythromycin and its derivatives (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Eslicarbazepine acetate can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The net effect on PPI action is unclear due to opposing CYP450 actions, so monitoring for gastrointestinal symptoms is recommended. Etravirine can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Fluconazole can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Fluoxetine can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Fosphenytoin can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Grapefruit can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Hydrocortisone can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Indinavir can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Isoniazid can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP2C19 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Larotrectinib can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Rabeprazole can decrease levothyroxine levels by increasing gastric pH, with conflicting evidence regarding this interaction. Rabeprazole can also decrease liothyronine and liotrix levels by increasing gastric pH, with conflicting evidence and unclear clinical significance. Reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs can decrease the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, though the area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. Marijuana can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Rabeprazole can decrease methamphetamine levels by reducing Tmax, so monitoring for clinical changes is recommended. Methylprednisolone can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Modafinil can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Nafcillin can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Nelfinavir can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Nevirapine can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Oxcarbazepine can similarly decrease rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Pentobarbital, phenobarbital, and phenytoin can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Rabeprazole can decrease phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, with minor or unknown significance. Rabeprazole can decrease ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH, with unclear clinical significance. Posaconazole can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Primidone can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Quinupristin/dalfopristin can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Ribociclib can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Rifampin and rifapentine can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, respectively. Ritonavir can increase rabeprazole levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor or unknown significance. Rabeprazole can increase ruxolitinib topical levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Rabeprazole can decrease thyroid desiccated levels by increasing gastric pH, with conflicting evidence regarding this interaction. Voriconazole can increase rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Rabeprazole can decrease acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Due to the long-lasting effects of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate this interaction. Avoiding or using an alternative drug is recommended. Apalutamide, a strong CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 inducer, can decrease rabeprazole levels or effects by affecting these enzymes. Co-administration may result in lower exposure to rabeprazole, so alternative drugs should be considered when possible.
